subject: collapse() to triangle and align node label to edge of triangle

messages.author: aa76bc9ea2907e22
messages.subject: collapse() to triangle and align node label to edge of triangle
parts:
Hi group members,

I have been trying to collapse over 100 species OTUs in tree and then label them so that the label aligns with the edge of the triangle, but this is not done automatically with geom_nodelab() as it uses the x coordinate of the collapsed node to position the label. When there is a triangle it would be nicer to have the label at the edge of the triangle.

The only way I have been able to label the collapsed triangle at its edge is to get the x values directly from the polygon layer for each collapsed node and use geom_cladelabel() and "offset"

Is there a more automated way to plot labels of collapsed triangle nodes? It would be great to also account for whether the triangle is plotted with diffrent modes ("max", "min", "mixed")

Thanks

Peter

example below:

library(ggtree)
nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="treeio")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
p <- ggtree(tree) + geom_tiplab()
p

# collapse nodes
collapse(p, 21, 'max', fill='steelblue',clade_name = "Clade 1", alpha=.4) %>% 
  collapse(23, 'min', fill='firebrick',clade_name = "Clade 2", color='blue') -> p2 

# plot collapsed node labels - do not align - have tried using nudge_x, but it is not precise
p2 + geom_nodelab()

# only way to get correct position at end of triangle is to get it directly from the polygon layer use offset through geom_cladelabel
p2 + geom_cladelabel(21, "Clade 1", offset = max(p2$layers[[4]]$data$x) - min(p2$layers[[4]]$data$x)) + geom_cladelabel(23, "Clade 2", offset = max(p2$layers[[5]]$data$x) - min(p2$layers[[5]]$data$x)) + xlim(0, 60)
